minutes.headline: Planning Board denied the 101 Pleasant St right-of-way waiver and adopted standard stormwater, subdivision and site plan conditions.
minutes.summary: The board denied a partial waiver that would have narrowed the right-of-way at 101 Pleasant Street, citing the risk of the town becoming liable for the retaining walls. Four other hearings were continued to September 13, among them a 372,000 sq ft warehouse where traffic at the Leominster-Shirley Road and Reservoir Road intersection was the main worry. Who maintains stormwater structures came up on every project. The board also approved its letter on the Pond View 40B project and adopted standard conditions.

public_comment.topic: Concerned that drainage at 360 Flat Hill Road relies on individual homeowners and runoff will reach properties below.
A resident asked, via a relayed comment, whether pesticide residue from the former apple orchard would be addressed in the stormwater review.
A resident said the rain gardens sit where snow gets plowed onto them, the east side of Flat Hill Road already has drainage problems, and the lot 5 rain garden is close to the stone wall.

votes.motion: Do not approve the right-of-way waiver for the 101 Pleasant Street project.

Approve the three sets of minutes from July 26.
Approve the letter on Pond View Commons to forward to the town manager.
Adopt the standard conditions for stormwater, subdivision and site plan approval.

budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant said tax revenue from the warehouse would be significant and cited construction and permanent jobs.
Bright Farms donated to the open space committee after pulling out, and members noted the engineering work it paid for.

decisions.decision: 101 Pleasant Street applicant to return September 13 with the right-of-way at full width.
The chair would sign the Pond View letter; staff to send it to the town manager.
Staff will send the standard conditions to local engineering firms, post them online, and have the review engineer look them over.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted to deny the right-of-way waiver for 101 Pleasant Street; the applicant is to return September 13 with the right-of-way at full width.
Hearings on 101 Pleasant Street, 97 Cross Street, the Leominster-Shirley Road warehouse and 360 Flat Hill Road (scenic road and stormwater) were each continued to September 13.
The board closed the public hearing for 711 Massachusetts Avenue; the decision is set for the next meeting.
The board approved by voice vote its letter on the Pond View Commons project, to be signed by the chair and sent to the town manager.
A motion to adopt standard stormwater, subdivision and site plan conditions was made, but the outcome is not audible; staff will circulate them to local engineering firms.

why_it_matters: Who maintains stormwater structures, and whether the town could become liable for retaining walls, are questions that decide who pays for these projects' upkeep, which can end up as a cost to the town budget and tax bills.
Neighbors of the Flat Hill Road and warehouse proposals raised drainage and traffic concerns, and these hearings stay open until September 13 for public comment.
The standard conditions, if adopted, set the rules every later stormwater, subdivision and site plan applicant must meet, but the recording does not confirm the vote.
watch_next: September 13: continued hearings for 101 Pleasant Street, 97 Cross Street, the Leominster-Shirley Road warehouse and 360 Flat Hill Road, plus the 711 Massachusetts Avenue decision.
The town's official minutes, to confirm whether the standard conditions were adopted.
